# Review of audit PRs after #129 — 17 October 2026

Reviewed against `AGENTS.md`, the transaction-cart design contract, the context-complete workflow contract and the originating audit reports. The review pinned baseline `f61a66d6108a490234bb27da47384bd7eaafcf5b` and merged main `7c2239a5568429ccaa0f6cbc0d19c2c4f60ad2ce`, plus the original #151 and #152 heads. Independent standards and specification passes informed the findings.

Scope: #130–132, #135–138, #140–148, #151 and #152 (18 audit PRs). Bundle feature PRs #133, #134, #139, #149, #150 and #153 were excluded. No PR was merged during this review.

## Findings and repairs

| Origin | Finding and evidence | Repair |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #152 · P1/P2 | Actual Counter Quick Add for Rahman Hardware with the existing phone cleared the saved Bangla name/address and dropped a checked Vendor role. A real Tab/Enter journey also lost focus when Save removed the originating Add button. | Shared `quickAddPartyPreview` owns exact identity reuse. It merges every selected role, preserves existing profile fields and ledger sources, rejects ambiguous/inactive matches, and prevents replacing existing-role opening balances from a create form. Counter retains UI selection, translated feedback and explicit search focus after closing the child dialog. Updated in #152. |
| #151 · P1/P2 | A filtered Party → POS → Back journey lost the ledger and directory searches and date range. Completion dismissed into generic POS. New context copy was hardcoded bilingual. | A typed navigation snapshot preserves the Party workspace; explicit return and completed-preview dismissal share one return handler. New context copy uses the existing language preference. Browser coverage now completes a service-sale preview, returns by Escape, checks filters/range/scroll and mode-specific copy. Updated in #151. |
| Pre-existing Party range boundary | Selecting the shared This month preset caused `Statement To date cannot be in the future` and the page fallback. This preceded the audit diffs but blocked the new round-trip regression. | The Party range callback caps the end date at today and rejects future start dates with feedback. The shared calendar and ledger calculations are unchanged. Included in #151. |
| #136/#142 · P2 | Two accounts with the same name and number produced identical Counter transfer choices; the browser assertion observed one unique label for two records. Three account-label implementations had diverged. | Transfer pickers, confirmations and history now delegate to `financeAccountOptionLabel`, including its stable-ID fallback. The transfer utility retains a compatibility alias rather than another algorithm. |
| #142 · P1 | A newly recorded Counter transfer appeared as 06 Oct 2026 instead of its business date. The browser history-date assertion failed. The history adapter also omitted the entered reference. | Counter passes date and reference with stable endpoint IDs; Finance formats that date and retains the reference. Balance movement formulas are unchanged. |
| #137 · P1 | A Rocket expense saved with `accountId: undefined` and `method: 'bKash'`; the browser regression printed both wrong values. | A shared Counter-to-Expense adapter keeps source IDs and disambiguated labels. Only explicit bKash/Nagad provider metadata selects those provider names; other MFS accounts retain Mobile Banking. Expense correction preserves historical custom account choices and IDs when editing metadata. Validation, filters and reports share the supported-method list. A follow-up review caught the initially omitted report method, and the browser regression now verifies its translated row and amount. Legacy name-only payments remain supported. |
| #147 · P1 domain edge | With two same-name banks, one inactive, a legacy name-only cheque was unresolved for detail but clearance selected the active duplicate. A focused unit fixture reproduced the wrong identity. Current created/seeded UI cheques carry IDs, so this is not described as an ordinary UI reproduction. | Resolve uniqueness across all matching banks before checking active status. An explicit active bank ID remains valid. Existing cheque account-identity browser smoke verifies the normal ID-based lifecycle still works. |

No additional actionable regression was found in the reviewed shared Table wrapper, report printing, amount-in-words, POS price visibility or sidebar resize-target changes. This is scoped review evidence, not certification of every related workflow.

## Local verification

- #152: 129 unit-test files; TypeScript, lint (0 errors, 185 existing warnings), UI contract and build passed. Quick Add passed 48/48 Playwright journeys with 96 dialog axe scans after the focus fix. The focused keyboard/touch test checks exact profile/source preservation, all checked roles and focus return.
- #151: 128 unit-test files; TypeScript, lint (0 errors, 186 existing warnings), UI contract and build passed. The expanded Party → POS regression passed 48/48 journeys and 96 whole-page axe scans.
- Finance source corrections: 129 unit-test files; TypeScript, lint (0 errors, 185 existing warnings), UI contract and build passed. `npm run test:finance-source-review` passed 48/48 workflows and 48 scoped axe scans, including unique account choices, actual transfer dates/references, Expense source IDs/provider, metadata correction and translated payment-method report amounts. Existing duplicate-transfer balance/reversal regression passed, and the cheque account-identity smoke passed 2/2 journeys.
- Local combined source with the #151 and #152 corrections: 130 unit-test files, TypeScript, lint (0 errors, 186 existing warnings), UI contract and production build passed. Focused integration covered 6 Party/POS, 6 Counter Quick Add and 6 Finance source workflows, the keyboard identity regression, and duplicate-bank transfer balance/reversal. Additive package-command and type-import conflicts were resolved in the local test checkout. No GitHub PR merge was performed. The verified combined `src` tree is `2b3808884440ee1a4aa63be7c5f9adc309579f49`.
- Every full matrix uses 320×700, 360×800, 390×844, 430×932, 768×1024, 1024×768, 1280×800 and 1440×900; light/dark; English, English + Bangla and Bangla. Touch is used through 1024px. No force-clicks or arbitrary sleeps.

Existing build chunk-size advisories remain. Real software keyboards, downloaded-font rendering, manual screen-reader operation, persistent backend records and banking integrations remain unverified.
